**Problem Statement:** In aerospace design, the lift force generated by airflow over an aircraft wing profile can be modeled conceptually using the fluid circulation vector ($\vec{\Gamma}$) and the free-stream air velocity vector ($\vec{v}$). According to the Kutta-Joukowski theorem, the lift force vector per unit span ($\vec{F}_L$) is proportional to their cross product: $\vec{F}_L = \rho (\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma})$, where $\rho$ is the air density.

Let the air velocity flowing horizontally along the wing chord be $\vec{v} = \langle 150, 0, 0 \rangle\text{ m/s}$ and the circulation bound around the airfoil be $\vec{\Gamma} = \langle 0, 4, 0 \rangle\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$. If the air density at altitude is $\rho = 1.2\text{ kg/m}^3$, find the resulting lift force vector.

**Solution:**

1. Calculate the cross product $(\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma})$ using a matrix determinant:
    
    $$\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 150 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$$
    
2. Expand the determinant along the top row:
    
    $$\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma} = \hat{i}(0 - 0) - \hat{j}(0 - 0) + \hat{k}(150 \cdot 4 - 0 \cdot 0)$$
    
    $$\vec{v} \times \vec{\Gamma} = 600\hat{k}$$
    
3. Multiply by the scalar air density $\rho$:
    
    $$\vec{F}_L = 1.2 \cdot (600\hat{k}) = 720\hat{k}\text{ N/m}$$
    

**Meaning of the Answer and Engineering Application:**

The cross product yields an output vector of $720\hat{k}\text{ N/m}$. Physically, this tells aerospace engineers that the interaction between the forward air velocity vector (along the $x$-axis) and the structural circulation vortex around the wing (along the $y$-axis) produces a purely vertical lift force pointing straight up along the positive $z$-axis. Engineers use this spatial relationship to design wings that efficiently convert engine thrust into upward altitude-holding forces.
